ev.q: The 2022 adult immunization schedule summarizes ACIP recommendations, including several changes to the cover page, tables, and notes from the 2021 immunization schedule.

public_health_question.v: What vaccines and doses does ACIP recommend for U.S. adults aged 19 years or older in 2022, and what changed from the 2021 schedule?

ev.q: ACIP approved the Recommended Adult Immunization Schedule for Ages 19 Years or Older, United States, 2022.
new or updated ACIP recommendations for hepatitis B vaccine (HepB)
influenza vaccine ( 3 ), pneumococcal vaccines ( 4 ), recombinant zoster vaccine (RZV) ( 5 ), and COVID-19 vaccine
All recommended pneumococcal vaccines (i.e., PCV15, PCV20, and PPSV23) have been collapsed into one row.
RZV is now recommended for adults in this age group who have immunocompromising conditions.
recombinant zoster vaccine (RZV) ( 5 ), and COVID-19 vaccine
Changes have also been made to the human papillomavirus (HPV); measles, mumps, and rubella (MMR); meningococcal; and varicella (VAR) vaccination sections

equity.level_reason: A recommendation schedule with no data; age only defines the population (adults aged ≥19 years) and age bands in the schedule.

notes: Annual ACIP adult schedule describing changes from 2021; no quantities reported. Prepass cues are false hits: 'OR' is the conjunction in 'PCV15 followed by PPSV23 OR 1 dose PCV20', and 'CD4 percentages' are schedule thresholds, not outcomes.
